original.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Bangladesh general election held in February 2026:
items: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) defeated an 11-party Islamist alliance in the first elections held since the 2024 uprising.
BNP leader Tarique Rahman is the son of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Dhaka is seeking Sheikh Hasina's extradition from India for crimes against humanity.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Tarique Rahman is the son of the late former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia, and he returned after 17 years in self-exile. Hasina's extradition remains a sore point because New Delhi is still sheltering her.
original.source: Leader Tarique Rahman – son of the late former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia – now inherits a fractured nation after 17 years in self-exile.

rewritten.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Bangladesh general election held in February 2026:
items: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) defeated a 9-party Islamist alliance in the first elections held since the 2024 uprising.
BNP leader Tarique Rahman is the son of the late former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia.
Dhaka is seeking Sheikh Hasina's extradition from India for crimes against humanity.
rewritten.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
rewritten.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the BNP crushed an 11-party Islamist alliance, not a 9-party one, in the first elections since the 2024 uprising. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, and Hasina's extradition remains a sore point because New Delhi is still sheltering her.
rewritten.source: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) secured a landslide victory Friday in the first elections since the 2024 uprising, crushing an 11-party Islamist alliance.
